complete_compiler_story.headline: Safe model failover starts with replay boundaries

source.title: Designing failover across OpenAI model providers

read_evidence.scope: Complete production-routing guide: first- and third-party routes, private connectivity, route qualification, retry classes, deadlines, circuit breaking, gradual failback, ownership and a disabled-by-default implementation prompt.

source.freshness_reason: This 132-hour primary engineering guide is the freshest verified source found that supplies an end-to-end, testable provider-failover policy and remains within the allowed 168-hour extended fallback.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

complete_compiler_story.summary: OpenAI’s production-routing guide separates multi-provider availability from safe workflow recovery. Using a read-only fraud assessment, it permits failover only when retries are repeatable, deadlines remain, the secondary is approved and healthy, and features plus data controls match. Stateful sessions, partial outputs, unknown errors and uncertain actions require reconciliation or a safe stop.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Start with one read-only inference step. Centralize retry budgets, test both routes under load, block ambiguous replays and define queue, degraded or manual paths so an outage does not become duplicate work, policy drift or an uncontrolled provider switch.

complete_compiler_story.headline: Deep Agents keeps long-run context recoverable and inspectable

source.title: Context Engineering: How Deep Agents Remember

read_evidence.scope: Complete conceptual guide: context rot, tool-result offloading, recoverable summarization, on-demand skills, subagent isolation, long-term Markdown memory, provider switching, middleware defaults and customization limits.

source.freshness_reason: This 132-hour source is the freshest verified primary guide found that explains five recoverable context-management mechanisms together, and it remains within the permitted 168-hour fallback.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

complete_compiler_story.summary: LangChain describes five Deep Agents mechanisms for limiting context rot: offload large inputs to files, summarize older turns, load skills only when relevant, isolate noisy work in subagents and persist selected knowledge as plain Markdown. Summaries remain recoverable, and user-controlled storage lets memory survive a model or provider change instead of remaining trapped in one service.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Keep active context small without deleting evidence. Store raw outputs behind previews, preserve summarized history for retrieval, separate exploratory work and review persistent memory edits. This makes long-running agents easier to audit, migrate and correct when their retained assumptions become stale.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Other October 19 stories examine failover, modular models, governed knowledge, independent evidence and reusable procedures.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: A long-running agent moves bulky tool output into files, condenses old turns, loads skills on demand and delegates noisy research, while a recoverable memory ledger remains under user control.

complete_compiler_story.summary: OpenCode documents portable SKILL.md discovery across project, global, Claude-compatible and agent-compatible paths. Its git-release example pairs strict frontmatter with bounded instructions for drafting release notes, proposing a version bump and returning a copyable command. Pattern permissions can allow, deny or require approval, while manual-only metadata prevents accidental automatic selection.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Create a read-only release skill, test its name and discovery, deny unrelated internal skills and require approval before any publishing command. Compare generated notes with merged pull requests, keep version choice human-owned and never let the procedure push tags automatically.

complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable read-only release-note procedure grounded in OpenCode’s October 17 Agent Skills documentation. Create `.opencode/skills/git-release/SKILL.md` with matching lowercase-hyphenated name, a precise description, manual-only metadata and instructions limited to drafting notes, proposing a version and returning a copyable command. Set unrelated `internal-*` skills to deny and the release skill to ask. Test discovery plus one repository fixture; compare notes with merged pull requests. Return DRAFT, REVIEW or STOP, never execute a tag, release or push. Require explicit human approval for any later publishing command.
